newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq sets record high at close.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq sets record high at close.

text.p: Nasdaq stocks closed at a record high on Monday, bolstered once again by strength in the high technology sector.

But analysts said a closed bond market, due to the U.S. Veterans Day holiday, the heavy calendar of economic data this week and a meeting of the Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee put a damper on volume.
The Nasdaq Composite Index closed unofficially up 5.17 points, or 0.41 percent, to 1262.68, with advances leading declining issues by 2,099 to 2,015 on volume of about 439 million shares.
The previous record close was on October 16, when the index closed up 1.74 to 1258.10.

"High technologies seem to be leading the charge as usual," said Brett Discher, vice-president in charge of equity trading at Dain Bosworth. "Today is a bank holiday, so I don't think we're seeing the volume we would otherwise."
Data expected this week includes the producer and consumer price indices for October, as well as retail sales and industrial production and capacity utilization for last month.
"The market is getting over-extended and any little thing could cause problems," he said.
